identity.canonical_name_evidence: VERIFIED. 229 occurrences on the homepage, og:site_name, and the logo artwork itself.

name_conflict.where: site copy uses the singular; the Shopify vendor field on 249 of 250 products reads 'East Coast Art Studios'; product descriptions sign off 'Products by EastCoastArtStudios'

identity.positioning_line: Your favorite places, on your wall.
identity.category: Fine art prints of named streets and places, sold as gifts and home decor

logo.icon_mark_note: VERIFIED ABSENT. There is no symbol, monogram or icon anywhere on the site. Never invent one, and never render the brand as a badge or emblem.
logo.construction: Two tiers, centred. 'East Coast Art' in a high-contrast serif with fine hairlines and sharp bracketed serifs, sentence case. 'STUDIO' beneath in letter-spaced caps, roughly 0.3em tracking, at about a third the cap height of the line above.

defect_zero_padding.measured: Primary: opaque artwork runs to x=0 and x=1040, the full canvas width. Reverse: runs edge to edge horizontally, with 27% padding above and 17% below.
defect_zero_padding.consequence: Dropping either file into a layout with no added margin reads as clipped, and any auto-fit crop will cut the serifs.
defect_zero_padding.creative_rule: Add clear space equal to the cap height of 'E' on every side, in the layout. Never rely on the file's own padding, and never scale the two files to the same height: their canvases differ.

favicon.evidence: VERIFIED. https://eastcoastartstudio.com/favicon.ico returns 404 and no icon link tag is present in the served HTML.
favicon.creative_rule: Do not source a favicon from a third party or generate one. If an ad surface requires a square brand mark, crop the reverse wordmark to the 'E' or use a plain type lockup, and tell the client the favicon is missing.

palette.philosophy: VERIFIED by census of the theme CSS and the product photography. The brand is deliberately achromatic: white, near-black and warm neutrals. The artwork supplies every saturated colour. This is correct for the category and must be preserved.

palette.creative_rule: An ad frame carries at most two of these plus the artwork. If a layout needs colour, it takes it from the print, not from a palette swatch.

heading_font.evidence: VERIFIED. The theme loads playfairdisplay_n4 as a webfont and declares it on h1 through h6, on .header-logo__text and on .how-step__number.
heading_font.use: Every headline on an ad. It is the brand's voice in type and it matches the wordmark's high-contrast serif.

typography.pairing_rule: Playfair Display for the headline, Poppins for everything a reader has to work through. Never set body copy in Playfair: its hairlines disappear at ad sizes and on a phone.
typography.wordmark_rule: The logo is still PLACED as the supplied PNG, never re-typeset. Playfair is the heading face and closely resembles the wordmark, which makes a hand-set lookalike tempting and still wrong: the spacing and the STUDIO tracking are not reproducible by typing.
typography.correction_note: An earlier draft of this kit recorded the heading face as unidentified. That was a miss by a too-narrow search, not an absence. Corrected 2026-09-15 after the audit script's font census surfaced it.

social_proof.evidence: VERIFIED on a full 195KB product page load, 2026-09-15: no ratingValue, no data-average-rating, no aggregateRating JSON-LD, and the Judge.me widget renders no reviews. Judge.me is installed but empty. The Judge.me public store page 404s. Trustpilot returns 403, which is inconclusive rather than negative.
social_proof.consistent_with: MST Sprint 1 spent $57.97 of a ~$1,000 budget between 2026-07-14 and 2026-07-24 with ZERO conversions. A store with no conversions has no buyers to review it.
social_proof.ruling: The kit does not incorporate social proof because there is none. This matches the client's own rule, which already anticipated it: ship [VERIFIED COUNT] as a placeholder, NEEDS-VALIDATION, never invent a number.
social_proof.the_slot_is_built: Every prompt carries the placeholder convention, so a real figure drops in without a re-render the day one exists.
social_proof.how_to_close_it: The Judge.me admin shows the true count even when the storefront shows none. One number from the client closes this.

client_account_rules.source: VERIFIED. local_client_library.json v1.4.0, account_rules block. These are the CLIENT's rules and they outrank anything inferred from the public site.

offer.rule: Row D final line only, small type. NEVER in a hook or a headline, any row.
offer.why: A documented $40.54 cost per add-to-cart when this rule was broken historically. This is the single most expensive rule in the account.

client_account_rules.testimonials: Unattributed only, maximum 12 words, no fabricated named attribution.

conflicts_to_resolve.client_library_says: Made-to-order, real-wood-framed street/city MAP prints across 3,000+ cities
conflicts_to_resolve.live_catalogue_says: 1 of 250 products is a map. 162 are street sign, 139 oil painting, 8 cubism. The product is a painted city scene with a real street nameplate inside it.
conflicts_to_resolve.consequence: A model told 'map prints' renders maps. That is 16 wrong creatives and a wasted sprint.
conflicts_to_resolve.ruling: Render what the catalogue sells, not what the library says. Ask the client to correct the library.

conflicts_to_resolve.appears_in: copy_architecture.product_solution and PR_DataStat on the briefs
conflicts_to_resolve.live_evidence: The site's own meta description claims 200+ cities. 149 distinct places were counted across the 250 returned products.
conflicts_to_resolve.consequence: An ad claiming 3,000+ against a site claiming 200+ is an overclaim the landing page contradicts, which costs trust at exactly the moment the click is paid for.
conflicts_to_resolve.ruling: Do not render 3,000+ until the client evidences it. Substitute a claim that holds, or drop the count.

conflicts_to_resolve.field: real wood frame, real matte paper
conflicts_to_resolve.live_evidence: 228 of 250 descriptions state pine wood or metal framing and museum-grade 200gsm fine art paper.
conflicts_to_resolve.ruling: This claim holds. It is the strongest verified differentiator the account has.

icps.source: VERIFIED. local_client_library.json local_concepts. This corrects v1.0.0 of this kit, which recorded the CN_Design_* codes as defined nowhere: they are defined here, in the client's library, which the public audit could not see.

cvr_architecture.premise: This account has zero validated conversions. Nothing below is a proven lift: it is the set of things that remove friction, applied because the alternatives are worse, and each one is falsifiable by the sprint.

rules.rule: The product must be unmistakable in the first frame
rules.why: A painted street scene with a legible nameplate reads instantly as a specific place. A generic art print reads as a poster, which is the exact objection the hook is fighting.
The nameplate is the whole proposition and it is the first thing lost at feed size. If the street name cannot be read on a phone, the ad has no product in it.

rules.rule: Show the frame, not just the art
rules.why: Real wood framing is the verified differentiator and the price justification. An unframed crop competes on price with a poster.
The single most common unstated objection to wall art is 'how big is it'. Scene D and the size guide answer it without a word.
Made to order, real wood, real paper, free shipping and a discount in one frame reads as a clearance. Pick the one that serves the row's isolated variable.

rules.rule: The offer goes last and small, or not at all
rules.why: The client's own rule, with a documented $40.54 per add-to-cart when it was broken. Discount in a hook prices the product as cheap, against a brand whose entire argument is that it is not.

rules.rule: Land cold traffic on a collection, never a single product
rules.why: Client rule for C3, and it generalises: a buyer wants their city, and one PDP is a dead end if it is the wrong one.

cvr_architecture.proof_when_it_exists: The moment a real review count lands, it belongs in the same position across every cell, so the sprint measures the creative rather than the proof.
